messages.author: 6a93cd2e837d2d7b
messages.subject: Extracting values from McElreath's "rethinking" compare function
parts:
Hi all,
I recently upgraded my version of Richard McElreath's rethinking package, and now some code that used to work is buggy.

I had previously used the handy "compare" function to generate a table of AICc values that I could then extract:

> compare(N,M0,nobs=length(d[,y])) #this will generate:

k AICc BIC w.AICc w.BIC dAICc dBIC
M0 4 5446.423 5464.356 1.00E+00 1.00E+00 0 0
N 3 5493.882 5507.341 4.95E-11 4.63E-10 47.45926 42.98531

> C=as.data.frame(compare(...as above...) #This allows me to access AICc values via
> C$AICc

With the new version of rethinking, the output table still shows up ok in the console, but the line of code to convert to a data frame kicks out an error: Error in as.data.frame.default(compare(N, M0, nobs = length(d[, y]))) :  cannot coerce class 'structure("compareIC", package = "rethinking")' into a data.frame

Debugging through the source code, it looks like everything works fine until the last line of the source code, which assigns the output data:

> new("compareIC", output = result)

And with that, I am out of my league. It looks like he (Richard) is now designating the output as some new data structure called a "compareIC", which I assume he just made up. I don't quite understand all the data structure components to R, but it looks like if I make up a function and designate the data as new("data.frame", ...), then I can access columns like I want to. I suppose I could write my own version of the "compare" function, but I'd rather not, as I use the old compare function in many pieces of code. So, my question is:
Is there a way to coerce this unknown structure into a data frame, or otherwise extract values from it? I can provide the entire "compare" source code if needed. Thought I'd try DRUG first, then on to the author himself (unless he happens to be on this list serve?)

Cheers,
Jens

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Extracting values from McElreath's "rethinking" compare function
parts:
I think that what's going on is that as.data.frame doesn't know how to handle an object of class "compareIC". Since the object is just a data frame with a funny name, I think you should be able to fix it with: 

C <- compare(N,M0,nobs=length(d[,y]))
class(C) <- "data.frame"

If that doesn't work, Can you run 

C <- compare(N,M0,nobs=length(d[,y]))
dput(C)

and send the output?

messages.subject: Re: Extracting values from McElreath's "rethinking" compare function
parts:
Noam and Vince,
Thanks for the suggestions. Took me a while to get back to this, but you pointed me in some useful directions. I came up with a solution which I'll describe at the bottom, but first I'll respond to your suggestions.

So, to remind, C is a comparison table of 2 models:
>C <- compare(N,M0,nobs=length(d[,y])) #C is of some strange S4 class called "compareIC".

Noam, your first suggestion didn't work, but the class() and attr() functions were useful later on:
>
>class(C)
[1] "compareIC"
attr(,"package")
[1] "rethinking"
>
>class(C) <- "data.frame"
>C
Object of class "data.frame"
Error in getDataPart(object) :
  Data part is undefined for general S4 object

Noam, I didn't quite understand your second suggestion:
C <- compare(N,M0,nobs=length(d[,y])); dput(C) #and then send the output
Mainly because I still (after looking a bit) don't understand what dput does, or how to "send the output". But that is likely a conversation for another thread, unless you're itching to elaborate.

Vince, str(C) returns:
Formal class 'compareIC' [package "rethinking"] with 1 slots
  ..@ output:'data.frame':    2 obs. of  7 variables:
  .. ..$ k     : int [1:2] 4 3
  .. ..$ AICc  : num [1:2] 5446 5494
  .. ...#etcetera, more columns below

Any suggestions on how to interpret this? It looks like there's a data frame in there somewhere, but C$k, for example, returns
Error in C$k : $ operator not defined for this S4 class.
Nice to know about str() though.

My solution:
So, here's what I came up with after looking at the help files for class() and attr(). Just in case anyone's interested.
>
>C2=unclass(C) ; C2 #I believe this strips the "compareIC" class from C and reassigns it to a generic S4 object. Thoughts?
<S4 Type Object>
attr(,"output")
       k     AICc ... (more columns)
M0  4    5446.423
N    3    5493.882
>
>DF=as.data.frame(attr(C2,"output")) #attr(C2,"output) extracts the data-frame-like part from the generic S4 object C2, and as.data.frame reclassifies it to a standard S3 object of class "data.frame".

If anyone wants to elaborate on what exactly it is that I'm doing here, or if there's a more efficient way to do it, feel free to chime in. But for my purposes, this works fine now.

Cheers,
Jens
